paleobiology.scale_change: No named predecessor or successor chronospecies. Relative to a one-cell (~16 µm) domain the critical mode is inadmissible because L < lambda_c; on the 1.233 mm detail patch, N = L / lambda_c = 8. RCO and margin-growth modules change leaflet domain size at a larger scale and do not reset k_c.

model.name: Schnakenberg reaction-diffusion
model.kinetics: f = a - u + u^2 v ; g = b - u^2 v
model.boundary_conditions: Neumann no-flux on the rectangular detail patch. The specimen readout multiplies the field only inside the non-white leaf mask; the white background is not a reaction domain.
model.wavenumber_law: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)

state_variables.u: activator, read out as the dark core of a pigment ocellus

parameters.note: Operating point is just above the Turing threshold (critical D_v about 0.343 at this Jacobian) so the determinant-minimizing k_c and the maximum-growth wavenumber stay within a few percent. These coefficients are specific to slot 3140.

empirical_claims.claim: A two-species reaction-diffusion system with short-range activation and long-range inhibition selects a finite critical wavenumber k_c.
The cubic kinetics a - u + u^2 v and b - u^2 v admit a stable homogeneous steady state that diffusion can destabilize.
Cardamine hirsuta leaflet shape is produced by a quantified growth framework; the organ-scale domain is much larger than 154 µm.

RCO, present in Cardamine and absent from the Arabidopsis simple leaf, represses growth in sinuses and changes how many leaflets form. That changes domain length L, hence the mode count N = L / lambda_c, not the local k_c.

Cardamine trichome patterning uses a lateral-inhibition mechanism shared with Arabidopsis, so a periodic epidermal pattern at this tier is biologically real. The papers do not report a pigment-ocellus wavelength of 154.1 µm; that identification is the slot's quantitative target, not a quoted measurement.
